episode.title: Why a hydraulic cylinder pushes harder than it pulls
episode.subject: A double-acting hydraulic cylinder, 140 mm bore x 100 mm rod, at 350 bar implement pressure

sources.citation: Bosch Rexroth AG. Hydraulic cylinder, mill type, Series CDH1 / CGH1 / CSH1. Data sheet RE 17331/09.05. 44 pp. Mirrored by CMA/Flodyne/Hydradyne.
sources.locator: p. 1 (ratings); p. 3, table 'Areas, forces, flows', row piston AL 140 / piston rod MM 100
sources.quote: Nominal pressure 250 bar (25 MPa) ... Piston O: 40 to 320 mm ... Piston rod O: 28 to 220 mm ... [Areas, forces, flows; columns Piston AL, Piston rod MM, Area ratio A1/A3, A1, A2, A3, F1, F3] 140 | 100 | 2.04 | 153.94 | 78.54 | 75.40 | 384.75 | 188.40

sources.citation: Caterpillar Inc. 320 Hydraulic Excavator Technical Specifications. Distributed by Avesco AG.
sources.quote: Maximum Pressure - Equipment - Normal 35 000 kPa 5,075 psi ... Maximum Pressure - Equipment - Auto Dig Boost 38 000 kPa 5,510 psi ... Operating Weight 21 700 kg 47,800 lb

sources.citation: HW Part Store. 'Caterpillar 320C, 320 L & 320 S Excavator Boom Cylinder - Seal Kit' product listing. Retail parts catalogue, no stated provenance.

facts.claim: The implement hydraulic circuit of a 21.7 tonne Caterpillar 320 excavator operates at a normal maximum pressure of 350 bar (35 000 kPa).

evidence.note: Caterpillar's own published specification. The 380 bar Auto Dig Boost figure is transient and is deliberately not used.

review.notes: Read off the PDF this session, not recalled.

facts.claim: A 140 mm bore with a 100 mm rod is a standard manufactured cylinder size, published by Bosch Rexroth.

evidence.note: Published in the CDH1/CGH1 areas-and-forces table as a catalogue size.

review.notes: Narrowed 2026-09-18: the claim previously also said 'and used as an excavator boom cylinder', which only S003 (TIER-5) supported while the fact was marked verified. That application claim lives in F003, where its weak evidence is declared. The previous brief's 120 x 80 was unsourced and is not a size any source ships.

facts.claim: The specific cylinder modelled in this video is the boom cylinder of a Caterpillar 320C/320L/320S, Cat part 2590702.

evidence.note: The only source that makes this claim, and it is a retail parts listing.
Caterpillar's own 44-page specification publishes no cylinder bore or rod anywhere.

facts.what_would_settle_it: The Caterpillar parts catalogue (SIS) entry for cylinder 2590702, or a 320C workshop manual giving boom cylinder bore and rod.

review.notes: Deliberately not narrated. The script says 'an excavator' and never names the machine, so the weak claim is never made to the viewer.

facts.claim: For a 140 mm bore and 100 mm rod, the piston area is 153.94 cm2 and the annulus area is 75.40 cm2.

evidence.note: Both figures are printed by the manufacturer. Independently derived from the geometry this session as 153.94 and 75.40 - agreement to 0.002 cm2.

review.notes: These two numbers are the harness assertion: GEN cylinder derives them and must match the printed table.

facts.claim: The standard piston rod is the bore divided by the square root of two, which puts half the piston's area under the rod and leaves half as the annulus. Rexroth publishes an area-ratio column; the standard series measures 1.96 to 2.08 across the range, so a realised cylinder lands within a point of half rather than exactly on it.

evidence.note: Rexroth prints the area ratio A1/A3 in its own column and offers every bore with two rods; the standard series measures 1.96-2.08, i.e. rod/bore = 0.700-0.720 against 1/sqrt(2) = 0.7071. 'The phi = 2 series' is our shorthand for that column, not a label observed on the document. The spread is rounding to stock rod diameters: 140/sqrt(2) = 99.0 -> 100 mm = 48.98%.
Four of Caterpillar's five 320 boom cylinder variants (120x85, 140x100, 150x105) fall on the same ratio; 160x95 is the slim-rod outlier.

review.notes: Restated 2026-09-18: 'exactly half' and 'manufacturers designate this the phi = 2 series' both overreached. Design intent is half; realised cylinders are within a point. Narration says 'half', never 'exactly half' - the on-screen callout reads 153.94 -> 75.40, which is 48.98%, and a viewer can divide.

facts.claim: At 350 bar a 140 x 100 cylinder extends with 538.8 kN (54.9 tonnes-force) and retracts with 263.9 kN (26.9 tonnes-force).

evidence.note: Supplies both areas. Rexroth's own force columns at its 250 bar nominal are 384.75 / 188.40 kN; derived from the same areas this session as 384.85 / 188.50, i.e. the vendor rounds.

review.notes: Force = pressure x area is arithmetic, not a claim needing its own source; both inputs are TIER-1. Replaces the previous draft's unsourced 395.8 / 219.9 kN.
